chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shummun from al-Asamm from Mis'mam said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I have land that is demanded of me, and they encourage me (to sell).' He said to me, 'O Abu Sayyar, do you not know that whoever sells water and clay and does not put his money into the water and clay, his money goes to waste.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I sell for a high price and buy what is more spacious than what I sold.' He said, 'There is no harm.'

key_terms.الْمَاءُ وَالطِّينُ: Water and clay (representing the essential elements of land improvement/value)
key_terms.ذَهَبَ مَالُهُ هَبَاءً: His money went to waste (became void/useless)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid sale of land in Shia jurisprudence regarding reinvestment?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the economic principle of maintaining asset value through reinvestment, warning that selling property without preserving its productive essence (water and clay) renders the wealth void. This ruling distinguishes between mere liquidation and strategic asset exchange, affirming that acquiring a superior or more spacious property is permissible, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on dynamic wealth management rather than static hoarding. The narration underscores the ethical obligation to ensure that capital remains productive and beneficial to the owner's livelihood.
